comment: Graduated assurance should retain a minimum security floor. The graduated-assurance approach appropriately allows countries with different maturity levels to progress. However, the guidance does not clearly distinguish controls that may mature over time from minimum security properties that should be present from initial operation of components processing identifiable or sensitive health data.

citation.section: Section 2.3 - Trust and Security, p. 36, lines 401-427.

public.text: Graduated assurance should retain a minimum security floor. The graduated-assurance approach appropriately allows countries with different maturity levels to progress. However, the guidance does not clearly distinguish controls that may mature over time from minimum security properties that should be present from initial operation of components processing identifiable or sensitive health data.
public.suggestedRevision: Define a technology-neutral minimum security floor across DPI-H. Assurance mechanisms may mature over time, but core properties such as actor identification/authentication, explicit authorisation, least privilege, confidentiality, auditability, integrity/provenance, incident containment and secure recovery should not become optional solely because technical maturity is lower. Where stronger assurance cannot yet be achieved, residual risk and compensating controls should be documented.
